MAJOR_FINDING_supersedes_phase1_diagnosi.headline: The anchor absence is NEITHER a source gap NOR a sparse/incomplete load. It is a county_fips MISTAGGING bug at staging: real, correctly-geolocated Microsoft ML footprint rows for both probe counties are already loaded into tx_building_footprint, but tagged with a NEIGHBORING county's FIPS code, which the writer's own county-scoped query (staged-footprint-join.ts:244, `fp.county_fips = $6`) silently excludes.
evidence_48021_bastrop: Phase 1 reported nearest staged footprint to 48021:34049 (1109 Pecan St) as 1615m -- that query was scoped WHERE county_fips='48021'. Re-run with NO county_fips filter: true nearest is footprint ml:ml-4336967 at 1.63 METERS, tagged county_fips='48287' (Lee County), not '48021' (Bastrop).
Within 200m of the anchor, any-tag count = 80, ALL tagged 48287. Within 200m, county_fips='48021'-only count = 0 (this is exactly what the writer sees -- reproduces the FAIL).

County-wide: footprints geometrically inside Bastrop COUNTY's own polygon (tx_county_boundary, ST_Intersects), grouped by their own tag: 48021 (correct)=24970, 48287 (Lee, wrong)=17200, 48055 (Caldwell, wrong)=7735. Only 50.0% of Bastrop's true building stock is correctly tagged.
Inside Bastrop CITY LIMITS specifically (tx_city_boundary polygon): any-tag=3987, county_fips='48021'-only=1182 (29.6% correctly tagged, 70.4% invisible to the writer).

Independently verified against the live public Microsoft Global ML Building Footprints source (no credential; https://minedbuildings.z5.web.core.windows.net/global-buildings/dataset-links.csv manifest, tile RegionName=UnitedStates quadkey=023130123, downloaded and parsed directly, 82777 features): centroid-based nearest-to-anchor = 13.77m, within-200m count = 78, centroids inside Bastrop's city bbox = 8356. All consistent with what's already loaded in cortex -- the SOURCE is dense here; nothing needs to be bought.
evidence_48453_travis_west_lake_hills: Probe parcel 48453:113408 (414 Spiller Ln, West Lake Hills): true nearest footprint (any tag) is 0m (contains the point), tagged county_fips='48209' (Hays County), not '48453' (Travis). County_fips='48453'-only nearest is 7463-7480m -- matches phase 1's cited 7464.2m exactly, confirming that figure was itself an artifact of the same bug.

West Lake Hills city limits (tx_city_boundary): ALL 1693 footprints geometrically inside the city are tagged 48209 (Hays), ZERO are tagged 48453 (Travis) -- a complete (100%), not partial, mistagging for this town.
This is the same class of bug as Bastrop/Lee/Caldwell, in the opposite direction (Hays instead of Lee/Caldwell) -- confirms a systemic staging defect, not a one-off data error.
why_this_is_a_LOAD_defect_not_a_source_g: Total staged row counts per county (48021=65974, 48453=73394) and statewide (10674975, 254 counties) match the 2026-08-19 reading exactly -- the load's VOLUME has not changed and is not partial in the sense of 'rows missing'.
The already-loaded rows ARE the correct geometry at the correct location (confirmed independently against Microsoft's own live public tile for Bastrop) -- the source captured these buildings.

The only defect is the county_fips VALUE attached to each row at staging time, which appears to use a coarse (likely bounding-box) method rather than true point/polygon containment -- landing_parcel_jurisdiction (a different, parcel-side table) already does correct ring/point-in-polygon jurisdiction assignment elsewhere in this same program, which is evidence this is a fixable loader defect, not a source-side limitation.

This falls on the LOAD side of the ruling's binary (reload via P-169's job from the SAME dataset, no second source), but is a narrower and more precise mechanism than 'partial/incomplete load volume': it is a MISTAGGING defect. P-169's job must assign county_fips by true geometry containment against tx_county_boundary (or equivalent), not reproduce whatever method produced this result, or the same bug recurs verbatim.

falsifierResult: Pre-registered: 'if the count inside Bastrop city limits is within an order of magnitude of the town's building count AND the anchor still has no polygon within 200m, the load-gap reading is wrong and the source-gap reading stands.' OBSERVED: city-limits count (3987 any-tag, cross-checked at 8356 centroids via the independent live Microsoft tile) IS a plausible, town-appropriate order of magnitude -- AND the anchor DOES have a polygon within 200m (1.63m nearest) once measured without the county_fips-filter bug. The falsifier's own trigger condition ('still no polygon within 200m') is FALSE, so it does not fire against the load-gap reading. Source-gap is decisively ruled out for both probe parcels.
